# Literature review — Compiler/execution feedback for model training; compilation environments and execution world models; efficient Lean compilation for RL feedback

*Generated by `kb.py render` on 2026-09-23. Do not edit; edit `refs.jsonl` / `notes/` and re-render.*

**Research questions**

1. How is compiler / execution / verifier feedback used as a training signal for code and proof models (RL from execution, expert iteration, repair), and where does it fail?
2. How are compilation/execution environments built at scale for training (sandboxes, Lean interaction tools), and can learned world models of execution/compilation substitute for or augment them?
3. What makes Lean verification fast enough for RL feedback (REPL state reuse, environment pickling, incremental elaboration, parallel verifier servers), and what throughputs are reported?

## Read, by trust tier

Tier is the reader's judgement after reading (`trust-rubric.md`); `prior` is the metadata-only starting point. Quotes: ✅ every block quote found in the archived text, ❌ one is not, ✋ no archived text — hand-checked only.

### T1 established (4)

| key | work | venue | year | rel | quotes | why this tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `olausson2023self` [notes](notes/olausson2023self.md) | Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation? | arXiv (Cornell University) | 2023 | 3 | ✅ | ICLR 2024; code/data released; matched-budget i.i.d. baseline incl. token variants. Now independently confirmed in Lean at matched verifier calls (lin2025goedela: self-correction ≈0–0.5 pp over resampling) and consistent with gehring2024rlef (untrained models gain nothing from feedback) (was T2; see lin2025goedela) |
| `xin2024deepseeka` [notes](notes/xin2024deepseeka.md) | DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5: Harnessing Proof Assistant Feedback for Reinforcement Learning and Monte-Carlo Tree Search | arXiv (Cornell University) | 2024 | 3 | ✅ | ICLR 2025; standard baseline across the field; released weights. Tier kept T1 for the work as a whole, but its claim that RL gives a budget-stable "genuine enhancement" is now [C] vs yue2025does (RLVR narrows pass@k at large k) and lin2025goedela (RL lowers pass@32, needs weight averaging) |
| `yang2023leandojo` [notes](notes/yang2023leandojo.md) | LeanDojo: Theorem Proving with Retrieval-Augmented Language Models | arXiv (Cornell University) | 2023 | 3 | ✅ | NeurIPS 2023 D&B (stated in text); code/data/models released; standard baseline and toolkit widely reused; single-run eval, headline on easy random split |
| `polu2022formal` [notes](notes/polu2022formal.md) | Formal Mathematics Statement Curriculum Learning | arXiv (Cornell University) | 2022 | 2 | ✅ | ICLR 2023 (notable top-25%, confirmed on OpenReview; archived text is arXiv v1 preprint); expert iteration is the standard baseline extended by DeepSeek-Prover and Goedel-Prover; lean-gym released; caveats: compute-matched claim uses fitted adjusted-compute curve, single runs, lean-gym 21.1% false negatives (yang2023leandojo) bias results downward |
